title: What Got Through
scopeNote: This keeps the performed two-stream task and the two probes that follow it, which together are the finding the selection theories were built around. The harder attended task used to shift the pattern, the naive first trial, the simulated class data and the theory-by-theory prediction table stay in the longer version, and the page says so.
summary: Two streams of words arrive side by side. The learner has a job to do with one of them and is told to ignore the other entirely, then answers two questions about the ignored stream: whether it changed, and what it was about. The two answers usually come apart.
learningObjectives: Distinguish detecting a physical change in an ignored channel from identifying its meaning.
Explain which findings early selection, attenuation and late selection were each built to handle.
Explain why failure to report is weak evidence for absence of processing.
Recognise why a theory that accommodates every finding is not thereby supported by them.
Recognise the limits of a visual analogue of a listening task.
interactionTypes: a performed two-stream task with a target-detection load on the attended stream
a scored attended task so the learner can see whether they were attending
two probes about the ignored stream, the second withheld until the first is answered
feedback that differs by which of the four outcome patterns occurred
a skip route that reaches the same finding without performing the task
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every response is scored in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: The attended response works from the space bar or a labelled button. The display description names the attended word on each pair and states that an ignored word is also present, but never reads the ignored word aloud: doing so would hand a screen-reader user the answer to the second probe. Because the task requires seeing two columns at once, and a screen reader necessarily serialises them, a skip route is offered from the start and reaches the same finding and the same explanation; the page says why it exists. Nothing flashes or moves and the words change about once a second. The probes are keyboard operable and marked with a glyph and a hidden note as well as a colour. Every stage is announced through a polite live region.
dataStatus: Invented word lists. The attended list contains five colour words as targets; the ignored list is 24 kitchen items, none longer than nine characters so that no word runs outside the panel. Nothing is a norm.
simulationNotes: 24 pairs at about one a second. The ignored column switches from lower case to capitals at pair 15, which is the physical change: it has to be something detectable without any word having been recognised, and case does that where a colour change would put the demonstration behind colour vision. The attended task is a genuine detection load rather than a decorative instruction, because without something to do there is nothing being divided; the hit rate is reported so a learner can see whether they were attending, and a poor hit rate makes their probe answers uninterpretable rather than wrong. All four outcome patterns are handled in their own words, including the awkward ones: catching both is attributed to the attended task not occupying the learner, catching neither is called a stronger result rather than a worse one, and catching the category without the case change is met with scepticism about a one-in-four guess.
readmeTopic: what survives from a stream you are ignoring, and what the selection theories were built to explain
